title: Avoiding Parallel Simon's Quadratic Qubit Blowup
summary: Parallel Simon uses quadratic qubit space rather than ordinary Simon's linear input space; whether subquadratic space can preserve the speedup, including in the FX attack, remains open.

formal_statement.body: For quantum algorithms that exploit parallel computation---such as the parallel variant of Simon's algorithm and the Grover--Simon attack on the FX construction---determine whether the quadratic space blowup (from $O(n)$ input bits to $O(n^2)$ qubits in Simon, or from $m+O(n)$ to $m+O(n^2)$ in the FX attack) can be reduced to $o(n^2)$ while preserving the parallel speedup. In particular, for the Grover--Simon attack on FX, determine whether the attack can be carried out using $m+o(n^2)$ qubits, improving on the analysis suggesting that roughly $m+2n^2$ qubits suffice.

scope.domain: Quantum space complexity of parallel Simon's algorithm and Grover--Simon cryptanalysis of the FX construction.
parameters: n: problem-size parameter governing the asymptotic space bounds
m: additive parameter in the FX attack's qubit bounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether parallel computation can preserve its speedup with an n-dependent qubit term below quadratic, particularly whether the FX attack can use m plus a subquadratic term.

citations.label: Grover Meets Simon - Quantumly Attacking the FX-construction

progress.summary: The source contrasts ordinary Simon's linear input requirement with the parallel variant's quadratic qubit requirement and explicitly leaves avoidance of this blowup as an open problem.
citation_labels: Gregor Leander et al., Grover Meets Simon - Quantumly Attacking the FX-construction
